extracted.intended_audience: readers, subscribers, and potential contributors to The Forerunner; persons interested in Charlotte Perkins Gilman's social-literary project
extracted.subtask_description: Editorial and publication guidance for The Forerunner (Charlotte Perkins Gilman's monthly), describing purpose, themes, acceptable content types, advertising policy, and departmental limits. Useful for potential contributors, advertisers, and readers evaluating the magazine's aims and standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: It is written entirely by Charlotte Perkins Gilman.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Forerunner's content is produced solely by the editor/owner; contributors are not indicated—this is a single-author monthly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose — stimulate thought and practical change
rubrics_metrics.description: It is to stimulate thought: to arouse hope, courage and impatience; to offer practical suggestions and solutions, to voice the strong assurance of better living, here, now, in our own hands to make.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Material should aim to provoke thought and to promote practical, immediate improvements in life; rhetoric and content should be mobilizing rather than merely ornamental.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thematic focus — people, principles, everyday life
rubrics_metrics.description: It is about people, principles, and the questions of every-day life; the personal and public problems of to-day. It gives a clear, consistent view of human life and how to live it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptable pieces focus on human experience and social/practical questions; clarity and consistency in presenting a view of life and conduct are expected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of treatment — man, woman, and child
rubrics_metrics.description: It will treat all three phases of our existence--male, female and human. It will discuss Man, in his true place in life; Woman, the Unknown Power; the Child, the most important citizen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The magazine is not narrowly a 'woman's magazine'—it deliberately addresses multiple social roles and perspectives; submissions should consider these three phases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ideological stance — socialization/Socialism as part of mission
rubrics_metrics.description: It is a magazine for humanity, and humanity is social. It holds that Socialism, the economic theory, is part of our gradual Socialization, and that the duty of conscious humanity is to promote Socialization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content sympathetic to socialization/socialist ideas (as part of human social progress) is aligned with the magazine's mission; explicit or implicit support for social reform is appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertising policy — truth and personal experience preferred
rubrics_metrics.description: In its advertising department, under the above heading, will be described articles personally known and used. So far as individual experience and approval carry weight, and clear truthful description command attention, the advertising pages of The Forerunner will be useful to both dealer and buyer. If advertisers prefer to use their own statements The Forerunner will publish them if it believes them to be true.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advertising should be truthful; personal-knowledge endorsements are preferred. The editor will vet advertiser claims and will only publish outside statements she judges true.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content types and regular features
rubrics_metrics.description: It is a monthly magazine, publishing stories short and serial, article and essay; drama, verse, satire and sermon; dialogue, fable and fantasy, comment and review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each issue is expected to include a mix of formats (novel/serial, book-length studies, short stories, essays, poems, sermons, reviews). Submissions (if any) should conform to these types and the magazine's variety-driven structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal Problems department limits
rubrics_metrics.description: The department of 'Personal Problems' does not discuss etiquette, fashions or the removal of freckles. Foolish questions will not be answered, unless at peril of the asker.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Q&A ('Personal Problems') section excludes trivial/foolish topics; questions should be substantive and about real personal/public problems, not mere etiquette or cosmetic concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial topic exemplars / preferred article subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: The main feature of the first year is a new book on a new subject ... 'Our Androcentric Culture.' ... Among the short articles will appear: 'Private Morality and Public Immorality.' 'The Beauty Women Have Lost' 'Our Overworked Instincts.' 'The Nun in the Kitchen.' 'Genius: Domestic and Maternal.' 'A Small God and a Large Goddess.' 'Animals in Cities.' 'How We Waste Three-Fourths Of Our Money.' 'Prize Children' 'Kitchen-Mindedness' 'Parlor-Mindedness' 'Nursery-Mindedness'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preferred topics investigate gender, domestic economics, cultural critique, and practical social problems; submissions aligned with these themes are suitable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetry standard — substance plus form
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the poetry have bones to it as well as feathers?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Poems should combine formal beauty ('feathers') with substantive meaning or intellectual/moral backbone ('bones'); mere prettiness is insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value proposition — expected annual contents for subscribers
rubrics_metrics.description: If you take this magazine one year you will have: One complete novel ... One new book ... Twelve short stories ... Twelve-and-more short articles ... Twelve-and-more new poems ... Twelve Short Sermons ... Besides 'Comment and Review' ... 'Personal Problems' ... And many other things ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subscribers should expect a steady, specified quantity and variety of original material annually; editorial planning aims to deliver that content mix each year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience test — publish because there are enough persons interested
rubrics_metrics.description: It is published to express ideas which need a special medium; and in the belief that there are enough persons interested in those ideas to justify the undertaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The magazine's viability is contingent on a readership invested in its ideas; content should therefore target and appeal to a committed audience for social-literary reform.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writer/reader cultivation — enlarge range of consciousness
rubrics_metrics.description: And so enlarge your range of consciousness, thinking, talking, reading about big human interests, that your own trouble shrinks in proportion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The magazine advocates broad reading/thinking about major human interests; contributors and readers are encouraged to engage widely with big social and human topics rather than narrow personal concerns.
